entries.name: Restricted Boltzmann Machine Collaborative Filtering
entries.definition: A family of shared-parameter restricted Boltzmann models for categorical user-item ratings, with a user-specific visible set and optional conditioning on the item-observation mask and low-rank factorization of rating interactions.
entries.identity_notes: This record denotes the specific mask-indexed rating construction and its conditional/factored variants in Salakhutdinov, Mnih and Hinton 2007. It is narrower than a generic RBM application or the maintained input-conditioned RBM architecture. Corresponding item/rating parameters are shared across users, but each observed-item set defines its own joint law. It is not a single trained Netflix model, a matrix-factorization predictor, the generic CRBM, or a standalone ensemble-performance record. Gaussian hidden units with unit variance are a source variant; the defining displayed mechanism below uses binary hidden units. Four candidate identities were compared against all 442 pinned AIO IDs, labels and scoped synonyms and 447 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. evidence_sources.title: Restricted Boltzmann Machines for Collaborative Filtering
evidence_sources.version: Eight-page author-hosted ICML 2007 paper, proceedings pp. 791-798. All eight PDF pages visually read; no numeric printed page labels. Andriy Mnih is the author named on the title page, distinct from Volodymyr Mnih of the later generic CRBM paper.

claims.statement: For a user with included item set S, let v_ik be one-hot over K possible ratings and h_j be binary. Define E_S(v,h)=-sum_(i in S,k,j) v_ik W_ikj h_j-sum_(i in S,k) b_ik v_ik-sum_j c_j h_j, and normalize exp(-E_S) over those rating groups and hidden states. Finite support gives a finite partition for finite parameters. Rating groups given h have softmax probabilities and hidden units given v have independent sigmoid probabilities. Parameters W,b,c are shared across users; missing-item terms are omitted. Omitting an item is generally different from integrating it out of a larger fixed-item model, because that integration introduces a hidden-dependent factor. The discovery calculation verifies this distinction on a finite example. Rating-category coding does not itself encode an ordinal likelihood.

evidence.locator: Section 2.1, Equations 1-4 and Figure 1, PDF pp. 1-2; omitted-item statement following Equation 4

claims.statement: For one added query item q, let a_j=c_j+sum_(i in S,k) v_ik W_ikj. Its exact unnormalized rating score under the augmented visible-set model is exp(b_qk) product_j[1+exp(a_j+W_qkj)]. Normalize the K scores, then choose a mode or expected numeric rating according to the decision loss. This sums binary hidden states analytically. Multiple query items generally become dependent, and the paper enumerates K^n assignments for a joint n-item query. The experimental predictor instead computes hidden means sigmoid(a_j) from observed ratings and plugs them into a query softmax. That faster approximation generally differs from the exact scores; finite calculations exhibit a probability gap.

evidence.locator: Section 2.3, Equations 7-10, PDF p. 3

claims.statement: The conditional variant holds fixed a binary item-observation vector r and replaces c by c+D^T r. It represents p(v,h|r), not p(r). The source uses known test user-item pairs with withheld rating values as mask information. The factored variant writes W_ikj=sum_c A_ikc B_cj, restricting the flattened rating-interaction matrix to rank at most C and reducing parameter count. It does not impose that rank on the nonlinear predicted rating matrix; the conditioning matrix D remains separate. These variants preserve categorical rating support while changing conditional parameterization.

evidence.locator: Sections 4-5, Equations 12-14 and Figure 2, PDF pp. 3-5

claims.statement: Training averages user-specific sufficient-statistic updates for shared parameters and uses data-started contrastive divergence that reconstructs included rating groups. Finite CD is an approximate learning rule, not an exact likelihood-gradient guarantee. The reported Netflix comparisons distinguish ordinary, Gaussian-hidden, conditional and factored models, use different latent dimensions, and compare validation RMSE. The combined RBM/SVD result is a validation-tuned ensemble result; it does not establish a universal advantage for this model family.

evidence.locator: Section 2.2, Equations 5-6, PDF pp. 2-3; Sections 6-7 and Figures 3-4, pp. 5-6

limitations: Mask-indexed partitions and omitted-item joints do not automatically form a projectively consistent full-item distribution. Exact single-query inference is defined using an augmented visible set; neither arbitrary missing-data marginalization nor independent multiple-query predictions follows.

Mask conditioning uses which user-item pairs are known to exist, including test pairs in the source protocol. This transductive availability information is distinct from the withheld rating values; performance cannot be transferred to settings lacking that information without evaluation.

The Gaussian-hidden variant fixes variance to one. Its general displayed energy includes reciprocal standard-deviation scaling absent from the visible-conditional display; no arbitrary-variance implementation is certified here.
Short-chain CD can be biased, and increasing chain length is not evidence that a particular run mixed. Weight decay, latent dimensions, batch sizes and approximate prediction affect comparisons.

The paper uses the historical Netflix split, validation tuning and an ensemble with separately fitted SVD models. Autoencoder fine-tuning and deeper extensions are prospective in this paper. No author implementation or benchmark was run.

aio_mappings.rationale: The user-item probability family is a specific mathematical representation within the broader Model class.

The construction uses shared RBM rating distributions, including mask-conditioned variants. A related mapping preserves that component/family relationship without equating the complete mask-indexed construction to one unconditional pinned RBM.

evidence_sources.title: Learning Sparse Topographic Representations with Products of Student-t Distributions
evidence_sources.version: Official eight-page NIPS 2002 paper in Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 15. All pages visually read; no numeric printed page labels. Official metadata lists Welling, Osindero and Hinton; the PDF groups Welling and Hinton under Toronto and Osindero under Gatsby.

claims.statement: For filter columns J_i and positive exponents alpha_i, define p(x)=Z^(-1) product_i[1+(J_i^T x)^2/2]^(-alpha_i), requiring 0<Z<infinity. Its energy is sum_i alpha_i log[1+(J_i^T x)^2/2]. Experts are factors in a joint product, not the marginal distributions of independent filter outputs. In the square invertible case, a change of variables reduces normalization to scalar factors and a determinant. The source only states positive exponents; curator analysis adds the necessary domain qualification: rank deficiency leaves an unpenalized direction, and even full rank with positive exponents is insufficient. In one dimension with identical nonzero filters, the exponent sum must exceed one half. An independent spanning subset whose individual exponents exceed one half is a sufficient condition, since remaining factors are bounded by one.

evidence.locator: Section 2, Equations 1-3, PDF p. 2; curator integrability deductions from those equations

claims.statement: Introduce positive u_i with joint density proportional to product_i u_i^(alpha_i-1) exp[-u_i(1+(J_i^T x)^2/2)]. Integrating each u_i yields the displayed factor up to an x-independent Gamma constant. Conditional u_i given x are independent Gamma variables with shape alpha_i and rate 1+(J_i^T x)^2/2. Conditional x given u is zero-mean Gaussian with precision J diag(u) J^T when positive definite. Integrating x instead couples u through the precision determinant; this is not simply a directed model with independent Gamma priors and Gaussian observations. Proper full conditionals do not by themselves prove that the joint normalizer is finite.

evidence.locator: Section 3, Equations 6-8, PDF p. 3; curator determinant/domain consequences of the augmented joint

claims.statement: The paper fits filters and exponents with approximate contrastive divergence, drawing latent scales at observed data and then reconstructed observations. In a square invertible system, inverse-filter transformation of independent scaled Gaussian variables gives the required conditional covariance. In an overcomplete system, exact sampling can use a factorization of J diag(u) J^T. The paper reports a faster pseudoinverse replacement as an approximation; it is not generally the exact Gaussian conditional. A curator example J=[1,1], u=(1,4) has exact variance 1/5 while the pseudoinverse shortcut gives 5/16. No historical code behavior is asserted.

evidence.locator: Sections 3-4, Equations 4-8 and reconstruction procedure, PDF pp. 3-4

claims.statement: Quadratic grouping replaces each squared response by sum_j W_ij (J_j^T x)^2 with nonnegative weights. This couples neighboring or learned groups of filter energies, while latent scales remain conditionally independent given x. Fixed local neighborhoods can induce topographic organization; learned groups need not follow a fixed spatial map. The paper separately considers powers beta other than two, whose conditional transform-coordinate distributions are generalized Laplace rather than Gaussian. Independent transform-coordinate sampling uses the square invertible case; a pseudoinverse does not make the overcomplete case exact.

evidence.locator: Section 5, Equation 9 and experiments, PDF pp. 5-6

limitations: Positive exponents, unit filter norms and a valid Gaussian conditional are insufficient universal normalization guarantees. Individual factors need not themselves be normalized densities. Probability-model claims are conditional on the stated joint being proper; the record does not certify all source-trained parameters.

Analysis filters in an overcomplete product are not the independent latent coefficients of an overcomplete synthesis model. Conditional independence of scales given x does not imply independent scale marginals or independent observed features.

The pseudoinverse reconstruction used in the reported highly overcomplete experiment generally changes the conditional covariance. CD and this additional approximation do not establish exact maximum likelihood or unbiased sampling.

The visual experiments use whitened natural-image patches, selected dimensions, norm constraints and particular fixed or learned group structures. Displayed filter organization does not prove a biological causal mechanism or general predictive superiority.

The denoising demonstration uses a complete filter set and a separate iterative MAP algorithm. Proposed overcomplete/grouped denoising gains remain prospective. No author code, empirical training or denoising benchmark was executed.

aio_mappings.rationale: The specific normalized continuous density is a mathematical model within the broader AIO Model class.
The augmented undirected density supports graphical conditional-independence reasoning. The pinned target is task-scoped, so this relationship is not asserted as model-family subclass membership.

evidence_sources.title: Learning Sparse Topographic Representations with Products of Student-t Distributions
evidence_sources.version: Official eight-page NIPS 2002 paper in Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 15. All pages visually read; no numeric printed page labels. Official metadata lists Welling, Osindero and Hinton; the PDF groups Welling and Hinton under Toronto and Osindero under Gatsby.

claims.statement: For noisy y, positive-definite noise covariance Sigma, fixed filters J, positive exponents alpha and nonnegative grouping weights W, minimize F(x)=0.5(y-x)^T Sigma^(-1)(y-x)+sum_i alpha_i log[1+0.5 sum_j W_ij(J_j^T x)^2]. Ungrouped factors use identity W. At the current x set gamma_i=[1+0.5 sum_j W_ij(J_j^T x)^2]^(-1), form D=diag(W^T(alpha*gamma)), and solve [Sigma^(-1)+J D J^T]x_new=Sigma^(-1)y. The bound log(t)<=gamma*t-log(gamma)-1 is tight at gamma=1/t; exact bound minimization therefore does not increase the fixed objective. Sigma positive definite ensures the linear solve is unique even if J is rank deficient. Interpreting F as a proper-prior MAP objective additionally requires the PoT prior to normalize.

evidence.locator: Section 6, Equations 10-12, PDF pp. 6-7; curator majorization and positive-definiteness consequences

claims.statement: The log-potential makes the full objective generally nonconvex. Monotone exact updates do not guarantee its global minimum, and MAP is not generally the squared-error-optimal posterior mean. A scalar proper-prior calculation with alpha=10, noise variance 1 and y=8.5 reaches distinct strict local minima from starting values 0 and 8.5, with objectives approximately 32.03555 and 32.08788. The higher solution cannot be globally optimal. This is a curator counterexample to a universal optimization guarantee, not a reported author experiment.

evidence.locator: Section 6, Equations 10-13, PDF pp. 6-7; curator finite calculation from the stated objective

claims.statement: In the source special case of square orthonormal filters, isotropic noise and identity grouping, the stationary condition separates into scalar cubic equations. Other structured cases require their own derivation. Multiple stationary roots require objective comparison; a root alone is not a global-optimum certificate. The source applies the procedure to overlapping transformed image patches and averages restored patches, using a complete set of filters learned on natural images. This patch-processing and preprocessing context is part of the reported denoising experiment, not a definition of all Wiener filters or evidence of general benchmark superiority.

evidence.locator: Equation 13 and Section 6.1, PDF pp. 7-8

limitations: The algorithm fixes filters, exponents and grouping weights while optimizing the clean observation. It does not fit the prior, estimate a noise model automatically or sample posterior uncertainty.
Descent follows exact auxiliary updates and exact linear solves for the same fixed objective. Approximate solves, changing parameters or a different noise model need separate analysis.

Nonconvexity allows initialization-dependent local minima. MAP and posterior-mean estimates optimize different decision criteria; the source description of MAP as optimal is not an unconditional minimum-MSE theorem.

The source reports a single displayed noisy-image comparison with known Gaussian noise, overlapping patches and matched whitening/DC handling. It does not establish universal denoising gains or the proposed future benefits of overcomplete/grouped priors.
No author software or empirical denoising experiment was run. Finite arithmetic checks verify mathematical boundaries, not historical implementation correctness.

paper_reading.name: salakhutdinov2007rbmcf
paper_reading.reading: All eight PDF pages visually read, including every equation, plot, footnote and reference. Numeric printed page labels absent; use PDF page locators.
paper_reading.identity: ICML 2007 author-hosted paper by Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Andriy Mnih and Geoffrey Hinton, pp.791-798, DOI10.1145/1273496.1273596. Andriy is distinct from Volodymyr Mnih of the later generic conditional-RBM paper.
notes: Sections1-2.1, PDF pp.1-2: one RBM per user has visible categorical one-hot rating groups only for rated items, binary hidden units and shared corresponding weights/biases across users. Missing-item energy terms are omitted. This is a family indexed by observed item set, not in general the marginal of one fixed full-item RBM. Each mask has its own partition; finite categorical/binary support ensures properness for finite parameters.

Equations1-4 p.2: rating softmax and independent sigmoid hidden conditionals follow the bilinear joint. Category numbers are represented nominally; taking the expected rating later does not impose an ordinal likelihood. Binary hidden conditional independence holds with all included ratings observed, not after an unknown rating is integrated.

Section2.2 pp.2-3: user gradients average shared sufficient-statistic differences. CD starts at data and reconstructs only included rating groups. Increasing steps does not itself guarantee practical mixing, exact ML, or that finite CD is an exact objective gradient.

Section2.3 p.3: an added query item has exact categorical scores exp(b_qk) product_j[1+exp(c_j+W_qkj)], where c uses observed ratings and hidden bias. K scores can be evaluated without enumerating 2^F hidden states. Joint queries need K^n configurations by the displayed enumeration. Normalized rating expectation and rating mode are different decisions. The actual experiments use a faster plug-in softmax of hidden means (Equations9-10), which is generally not the exact query law.

Section3 p.3: Gaussian hidden variant has quadratic hidden energy and is proper with finite categorical visibles. Equation11 uses W*h/sigma whereas the displayed visible conditional omits the reciprocal sigma; the paper fixes all sigma squared to1, where they agree. No arbitrary-variance implementation is certified.

Section4 pp.3-4: conditional variant supplies vector r of which items were rated, including known test user-item pairs with withheld rating values. It changes hidden bias to b+D^T r and does not generate p(r). This uses available transductive observation-mask information, not withheld rating labels. Constant shifts across all rating weights can encode missingness because visible sets differ; they are not a mask-independent gauge. An input-gradient imputation alternative is separate and approximate.

Section5 pp.4-5: conditional factored model W_ikj=sum_c A_ikc B_cj reduces parameters and restricts the flattened interaction matrix to rank at most C. It does not force the predicted user-item rating matrix itself to rank C; nonlinear hidden inference remains. D is a separate conditioning matrix. A,B changes of basis preserve W. Paper typically C=30, F=500 for factored, F=100 ordinary; this is not all variants under identical parameter budgets.

Section6 pp.5-6: Netflix training100480507ratings,480189users,17770movies; validation1408395ratings, test2817131pairs with unknown-half scoring. Mini-batches1000users,40-50epochs, CD steps increased. Validation compares models; adding validation to training changes test conditions. Figure3 ablations and Figure4 SVD comparison are scoped historical experiments, not universal ranking guarantees.

Section7 pp.6-7: SVD comparator optimizes observed-entry squared loss by gradients with rating-count-weighted parameter penalties, not a direct SVD of the sparse rating matrix. Learned linear combination of multiple RBM/SVD predictions uses validation-tuned coefficients; reported greater-than6percent improvement is ensemble RMSE relative to Netflix baseline, not a standalone RBM absolute percentage-point accuracy result.

Section8 pp.7-8: autoencoder fine-tuning and deep-generative extensions are future directions; layer-width wording does not independently establish universal monotonic likelihood improvement. No author code or Netflix benchmark was executed. References expose maximum-margin matrix factorization, multiple multiplicative recommendation models, privacy-preserving factor analysis, and weighted low-rank approximation as potential distinct leads.
paper_reading.disposition: Curate the mask-indexed collaborative-filtering family with ordinary, mask-conditioned and rank-factored variants in one record; distinguish its specified rating semantics from the generic CRBM architecture.

paper_reading.name: welling2002studentt
paper_reading.reading: All eight official PDF pages visually read, including equations1-13, all figures, experimental text and references. No printed page labels.
paper_reading.identity: NIPS2002 / Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems15. Official metadata lists Max Welling, Simon Osindero and Geoffrey E. Hinton; PDF groups Welling and Hinton under Toronto and Osindero under Gatsby. Preserve venue year2002 rather than deriving a year from later citations.
notes: Sections1-2 pp.1-2: product of Student-t (PoT) uses f_i(x)=[1+0.5(J_i^T x)^2]^(-alpha_i), energy sum alpha_i log(1+0.5z_i^2), normalized jointly. Experts are unnormalized factors, not independent marginal features or a directed synthesis dictionary. When J is square invertible and alpha_i>1/2, change of variables gives a noiseless Student-t ICA density with a determinant; overcomplete products differ from overcomplete independent-source synthesis.

Equation2 only states alpha_i>0, insufficient for properness on unbounded space. Rank deficiency leaves an unpenalized direction. Even full rank is insufficient: in1D total exponent must exceed1/2. A full-rank independent subset whose exponents all exceed1/2 is a sufficient domain since remaining factors are bounded above by1. This is a curator mathematical qualification, not a claim about uninspected trained filters. Complete-case normalized Student-t interpretation needs nu=2alpha-1>0 with scale sqrt(2/nu).

Section3 p.3: augmented joint is product u_i^(alpha_i-1) exp[-u_i(1+z_i^2/2)]. Conditional u_i|x are independent Gamma(shape alpha_i, rate1+z_i^2/2); x|u is zero-mean normal with precision J diag(u) J^T if positive definite. The implied marginal over u is coupled through determinant factors; it is not simply independent Gamma priors followed by a Gaussian draw. Proper-looking full conditionals alone do not establish a proper joint.

Sections3-4 pp.3-4: CD samples u at data then a reconstruction x and contrasts energy gradients. Square inverse-filter sampling is exact; overcomplete Cholesky sampling with the stated precision is exact. Replacing inverse by pseudoinverse as reported is an approximation generally yielding the wrong covariance. Curator example J=[1,1],u=(1,4) gives desired variance1/5 but pseudoinverse construction5/16. No implemented historical code behavior is asserted.

Section4.1 p.4:50000natural10x10patches, centered/PCA sphered with DC removed (99dimensions),50176filters, fixed alpha1 and unit filter norms, pseudoinverse sampler, weight decay/momentum; reported more-than500-fold overcomplete representation. Unit norms alone do not prove full rank or normalization. Selected filter images are not a denoising benchmark.

Section5 pp.5-6: grouped factors use nonnegative W and sum_j W_ij |J_j^T x|^beta. Beta2 retains quadratic/Gaussian conditional; arbitrary positive beta requires generalized-Laplace conditional in transform coordinates in the square invertible case. This generalization is not literally Student-t for every beta. W row-L1 constraints, positive log-parameter updates, fixed-neighborhood and learned-group variants are distinct. Fixed local neighborhoods on a20x20periodicgrid have400experts for169dimensional16x16patches; alpha1,beta2, weights1/9. Another complete169expert run learns W/alpha/J with beta1; learned groups need not have a prescribed spatial topography.

Sections6-6.1 pp.6-8: iterated Wiener filter (IWF) is a separate MAP optimization algorithm with a fixed PoT prior and Gaussian noise covariance Sigma. Majorize each log t using gamma*t-log(gamma)-1, tight gamma=1/t. Update gamma_i=1/(1+0.5 sum_j W_ij (J_j^T x)^2), D=diag(W^T(alpha*gamma)), then solve (Sigma^-1+J D J^T)x=Sigma^-1 y. Exact updates decrease the fixed objective, not necessarily to a global mode. This is inference on x, not learning J/alpha/W or sampling posterior uncertainty.

Equation13 p.7: only square orthonormal filters, isotropic noise and identity grouping yield independent scalar cubic stationary equations. Multiple stationary roots can exist, so analytic roots do not identify the optimal solution without objective comparison. MAP is not generally the minimum-MSE posterior mean; calling MAP universally optimal would be unjustified.

Denoising experiment pp.7-8: complete99expert model with unconstrained norms and noW groups, natural-patch training; single rock image Gaussian noise sigma20. Every overlapping10x10patch transformed consistently with training, outputs averaged; noisy22.0dB, Matlab adaptiveWiener26.9dB with optimal5x5neighborhood/known variance, IWF28.1dB. The1.2dB reported gap is one displayed case, not a universal or statistically replicated advantage. Overcomplete/grouped denoising is future work.

References p.8: Hyvarinen1999 sparse code shrinkage, HyvarinenHoyerInki2001 topographicICA, WainwrightSimoncelli1999 Gaussian-scale-mixture image statistics, StrelaPortillaSimoncelli2000 denoising, and ZhuWuMumford1997 minimax entropy models are candidate leads. Existing PoE/CD/AIS records and generic ICA contexts require deduplication.
paper_reading.disposition: Curate Product of Student-t as a model family and Iterated Wiener Filter as its separately named inference algorithm. Preserve properness and sampler boundaries; do not certify all displayed approximation schemes as exact.

notes: Introduction and image model pp.3311-3313/PDF1-3: sparse distributed amplitudes synthesize an image as a linear combination of learned basis functions; analysis filters and synthesis functions are not generally equal. Overcomplete refers to coefficient number exceeding effective input dimension. This is distinct from a PoT analysis-product density, and from a direct fixed feed-forward sparse autoencoder.

Probabilistic framework pp.3314-3315/PDF4-5: independent sparse coefficient priors and Gaussian observation noise define p(I|phi) by integrating all coefficients. Cauchy prior is exp[-log(1+a^2)] with beta1; general positive beta with that log potential needs beta>1/2 for a normalized unbounded scalar prior. Sparsity is a modeling assumption appropriate to sparse data structure, not a universal independent-component guarantee.

Learning pp.3315-3316/PDF5-6: replace the evidence integral by its maximum as an approximation; this loses posterior volume and admits dictionary-scale degeneracy. Alternate coefficient optimization and residual-Hebbian dictionary updates, separately adapting atom norms to target coefficient variance. Nonconvex log penalty and finite coefficient settling do not guarantee exact marginal likelihood or global optimum. Equation14 reconstruction term derivative has factor2 relative to penalty; Equation15 absorbs/scales the regularizer without explicit reconciliation, so do not silently certify identical lambda conventions.

Simulation pp.3316-3317/PDF6-7: ten512x512naturalimages, isotropic whitening times low-pass exp[-(f/f0)^4],12x12patches, drop very-low-variance patches,144atoms, code initializationphi^T I and conjugate gradients up to10iterations or less-than1percent energy change. Dictionaryupdates average100presentations; norm target follows image variance. This is a particular natural-image learning experiment, not a held-out downstream benchmark.

Results pp.3318-3320/PDF8-10: learned localized/oriented/bandpass functions,144pixelsbutapproximately100effective dimensions makes representation about1.5times overcomplete. Qualitative robustness and numerical convergence are reported observations, not proof of source identifiability or optimization guarantees. Sparse coefficients differ from raw filter responses. Figures7-10 show learned bases, frequency/orientation distributions, responses and receptive-field probes.

Discussion pp.3320-3323/PDF10-13: physiological predictions involve interactions among overlapping units and discrepancies in frequency distributions. Hypotheses about V1 efficiency and true image causes are not confirmed causal neuroscience. Sparse distributed and coarse population coding differ; model remains linear and single-stage, with translation/occlusion/hierarchical extensions proposed.

References and Appendix pp.3324-3325/PDF14-15: noiseless square invertible limit yields ICA change-of-variables determinant and Bell-Sejnowski infomax learning under matched output nonlinearity. This limit does not apply to an overcomplete inverse. Bibliography adds low-entropy recurrent coding(HarpurPrager), local anti-Hebbian sparse coding(Foldiak), exploratory projection pursuit(Friedman), and multiple-cause mixture(Saund) leads, subject to identity review.

native_neighbors.name: Product of experts
native_neighbors.definition: A probabilistic model family that combines expert factors over the same observations by multiplying their values and normalizing the product over the observation space.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes the general normalized-product construction, including latent-variable experts, rather than an arithmetic mixture, a training algorithm or a language-model-specific factorization. The original cooperative-learning setting does not require experts to be separately trained. AIO FactorizedLLM has Product of experts as a related synonym, but its definition and parent restrict it to large language models; that related synonym does not identify the general family. Logarithmic opinion pooling uses normalized exponent weights and has a separate aggregation scope. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 373 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared. The sole normalized hit is Product of experts as a related synonym of FactorizedLLM; its language-specific definition and parent distinguish it from the generic candidate. Both full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files and returned 59 lines each. All 29 unique matched contents were read; other hits concern citations, training components, prior boundary discussions or pending leads. All 88 semantic label/synonym hits, 20 exact fully annotated AIO nodes with outgoing edges, their generated records and four complete native neighbors were inspected or verified unchanged after previous full reading. Absence is bounded to this pin and inspected semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The normalizer must be finite and positive. Continuous expert densities being individually normalized does not alone guarantee that their product is integrable; nonoverlapping supports can also make normalization impossible.

Tractable inference within each expert does not make the product normalizer, model sampling or likelihood learning automatically tractable. Exact likelihood derivatives involve the full product distribution; short-chain CD is a distinct approximate learning procedure.

Experts need not use disjoint input dimensions, be individually well fitted, or produce a sharper or better calibrated distribution in every setting. A product of Gaussian factors remains Gaussian when well defined, so Gaussian factors alone do not represent arbitrary multimodality.

Conditional independence is between separate latent expert states given all modeled observations. Missing observations can couple the experts. The original architecture is not defined by a sparse router or an arithmetic average of expert predictions.

Unit exponent products and geometric opinion averages are not interchangeable: multiplying duplicate factors can sharpen a distribution, while identical distributions pooled with exponent weights summing to one remain unchanged. No empirical advantage or author implementation is certified.

claims.statement: For observations x, form p(x)=product_m f_m(x;theta_m)/Z(theta), with Z the sum or integral of the product over x and 0<Z<infinity. Expert factors may be unnormalized; multiplying one by a positive x-independent constant cancels in the final normalization. For parameters local to expert m, the exact log-likelihood derivative is its log-factor derivative at the data minus the expectation of that derivative under the full product model. In the latent-expert construction, f_m(x)=sum_hm f_m(x,h_m), and separate expert hidden variables are conditionally independent given a completely observed x, allowing separate inference when each expert is tractable. This does not imply independence of observed coordinates or independence of experts after some observations are marginalized. Restricted Boltzmann machines instantiate the family with one expert per hidden unit, whereas product HMMs use complete HMM sequence distributions as factors.

native_neighbors.definition: A conditional neural probability model that represents an output vector with an RBM whose biases or interactions are determined by a supplied conditioning vector.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is the general input-conditioned RBM family described by Mnih, Larochelle and Hinton, with their affine-bias binary formulation as the explicitly curated mechanism. The conditioning vector need not be temporal history. Autoregressive CRBM fixes it to earlier frames and RNN-RBM derives it from a recurrent state; these are narrower constructions, not aliases for the entire family. HashCRBM and CD-PercLoss are separate training or prediction constructions and do not define every conditional RBM. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in both worktree and main, returning 129 lines each. All 91 unique matched contents were read, including 58 initial contents and 33 additional saved-review contents: prior model contrasts, evidence references and discovery leads, rather than existing candidate identities. All 52 semantic label/synonym hits and 22 exact annotated AIO nodes were inspected, alongside corresponding generated records and four complete native neighbors. limitations: The model specifies p(v|u), not the input marginal p(u). Normalizing outputs for one conditioning vector does not supply a shared partition for every other input or a joint model over arbitrary inputs.

Factorial block conditionals do not make the output marginal factorial or its partition, joint mode and coordinate marginals generally tractable. Tiny output spaces or deliberately restricted support are special cases.

A small data-started CD update can reflect poor mixing near the observed output rather than accurate predictions from u alone. Finite CD is not generally the exact conditional likelihood gradient or the gradient of a single fixed objective.

Persistent samples from one conditioning input cannot simply be treated as equilibrium samples for another. The paper’s discussion of persistent-chain impracticality is scoped to its input-specific distributions and training setting; it is not a proof that every conditional persistent method is impossible.

The general family can condition biases or interactions, while the displayed mechanism holds W_vh fixed and changes biases affinely. Gaussian outputs, input-dependent interactions, retrieved-support HashCRBM and perceptron-style training need separate conventions. It is a Gaussian conditional-autoregressive representation of a multivariate normal law with a specified conditional-dependence graph. Intrinsic improper Gaussian fields and infinite-lattice extensions require separate existence or constraint conditions and are not exact aliases here. Spatial conditional autoregression is not temporal autoregression and is not the simultaneous autoregressive model obtained by treating the same local residual equations as independent noise equations. Gaussian-process regression conditions a process prior on training observations for prediction; this record specifies the finite graphical joint law itself. It can be used as a prior but does not inherently introduce hidden labels or independent observation emissions. A singular precision can describe an intrinsic improper construction only with additional interpretation or constraints; it is not the ordinary normalized Gaussian density stated here. An indefinite precision gives a nonintegrable quadratic model. Positive diagonal entries alone are insufficient.

Finite-graph eigenvalue bounds depend on the actual graph and boundary conditions. Infinite-lattice stationarity criteria are not automatically necessary finite-graph conditions. The source’s stationary or homogeneous examples do not require every finite auto-normal model to share those assumptions.
Missing precision edges encode conditional independence, not marginal independence or causal effects. A sparse simultaneous-equation matrix can induce additional precision edges.

Unconstrained conditional least-squares, coding-likelihood or pseudolikelihood estimates may leave the proper joint parameter domain. The Gaussian fitting objective and parameter identifiability depend on the specified mean, graph and interaction parameterization; existence of a covariance representation does not ensure identifiable scientific parameters.

The source’s wheat and plant examples expose aggregation, nonstationarity and model-fit concerns; a fitted Gaussian field does not establish a causal spatial mechanism or universal predictive adequacy. With common v_i=sigma^2, compatibility reduces to symmetric positive-definite B and covariance sigma^2*B^(-1). In contrast, the simultaneous equations B*(X-mu)=epsilon with independent epsilon~N(0,Lambda) imply covariance B^(-1)*Lambda*B^(-T) and precision B^T*Lambda^(-1)*B. For the proper conditional model, a factorization Q=C^T*C allows exact Gaussian sampling as mu+C^(-1)*z with independent standard-normal z.

native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes the customary contrastive-divergence update family, including CD-1 and CD-k, rather than only the formal difference-of-KL-divergences objective that motivated it. The number of transition steps is an algorithm parameter, not a separate architecture. limitations: A short-chain CD estimate is generally biased for the likelihood gradient and is not generally the exact negative gradient of the formal contrastive-divergence objective. A small objective or accurate reconstruction can coexist with poor global modeling when the chain mixes slowly.

The binary-RBM CD-1 field can have unequal cross partial derivatives, so it is not universally the gradient of any scalar objective. The inspected convergence paper also constructs cycling with a particular nonconvex regularizer; this is not a claim that ordinary L2-regularized CD always cycles. Existence of a regularized fixed point does not establish convergence to it.

Exact Gibbs transitions require sampled states. Conditional expectations can replace final sufficient statistics by Rao–Blackwellization, but feeding probability-valued states into later nonlinear transition conditionals defines a different approximation. Hinton Section 8 explicitly uses such a probability-valued visible reconstruction in its digit experiment; that variant is not silently equated to exact binary Gibbs CD.

The original simulations do not prove universal likelihood improvement, unbiased learning or global convergence. Their digit classification experiments also disclose test-set model selection; no reported ranking is adopted as a general property.

The algorithm is not tied to an RBM architecture, and the formal objective is not merely a difference of mean log likelihoods: distribution-entropy terms matter. No author implementation, training run or complete convergence theorem is certified.

claims.statement: For each observed example or minibatch, initialize a Markov chain at the data and perform k transitions with the model parameters held fixed. For an RBM, alternate sampled hidden and visible blocks, then compute hidden conditional expectations at the resulting visible configurations for the negative statistics. More generally, contrast derivatives of the unnormalized log model at the data and chain endpoints, treating the endpoints as fixed for the update. The motivating objective is C_k(theta)=KL(q_data||p_theta)-KL(q_data T_theta^k||p_theta). Its exact derivative also contains the parameter dependence of the k-step distribution; the customary CD update omits that contribution. With a fixed ergodic kernel and sufficiently long chains, the negative expectation approaches the equilibrium expectation; a short-chain update does not assume that limit has been reached.
